unresolvedReferences.description: Xiaojian, Daming and Taishi have no packet reign mapping; their dates are bounded AD 453–479 from the packet's Yuanjia end year and Liu Song polity end year, not converted.
Liu Huaizhen's unnamed father is created as an entailed intermediary from 祖 (grandfather) and 伯父 (father's elder brother).
Guo Zini (國子尼) is an allusion whose own era is not dated in the packet; bounded only as preceding the AD 451–453 speech.
從弟 (younger cousin) is kept as a kin-of edge; the degree of cousinship and the intervening parents are not specified, so no intermediaries are created.
Shengming, like Taishi, has no packet reign mapping; bounded AD 453–479 from the packet's Yuanjia end year and Liu Song polity end year.
世祖 (Shizu) and 太祖 (Taizu, 'the Founder') are the temple names used by this Qi history; they are kept as separate unnamed-in-chunk persons without outside identification.

Jianyuan, Yongming and Longchang have no packet mapping. They are bounded on or after AD 479 (strongly inferred) because they follow the Liu Song reigns and the packet's Liu Song polity ends in AD 479; Jianyuan 2 and 4 are counted from Jianyuan 1. No upper bounds.
上 in 上優詔 (s0093) may be Taizu or Shizu and is left unlinked.
The old man in yellow robes seen in Lingzhe's dream is a dream apparition and has no person row.
北使 (the envoy to the north) is unnamed and has no person row.
天子 in the physiognomist's prophecy is linked to Emperor Ming, with whom the prophecy was fulfilled at the Xinting feast (s0121).

Taizu's accession and the later events in this chunk are bounded on or after AD 479 (strongly inferred) because they follow Shengming 3 and the end of the Song mandate; the packet's Liu Song polity ends AD 479. The Song reigns Taishi, Yuanhui and Shengming are bounded AD 453–479, not converted.
The sender of the separate edict (別敕) in s0140 is not named and is not linked.
上 in s0162–s0163 is taken as Taizu, the reigning emperor after his accession (s0158).

三年 is read as the third year of Taizu's reign (era not named in the unit) and bounded on or after AD 481; later Yongming dates are bounded from that chain (Yongming 2 ≥ 482, 4 ≥ 484, 6 ≥ 486). None is converted to an exact year.
Xiang Yu appears only as a guardian spirit. The packet gives no date for him, so he gets only an upper bound (no later than AD 537) derived from Anmin's lifetime.
The mourning edict (s0198–s0203, which uses 朕) is attributed to Shizu as the reigning emperor, strongly inferred; 朕 is not linked as a surface.
The Prince of Jiangxia whom Xuanzai served is not identified with any named prince; the text gives no personal name.

帝 in s0237 (the emperor Xuanmiao reported to after leaving his province) is not named and is not linked; 帝 in s0235 is linked to Emperor Ming as the reigning emperor who suspected Taizu, strongly inferred.
The Prince of Yuzhang in s0226b (Song era) and s0242 (after Shizu's accession) is treated as one unnamed person; the text does not confirm the identity.
Taizu is taken as Shizu's father (parent-of, strongly inferred) from Shizu's words 父辱子死 in his report to the emperor (上) and Taizu's reply in s0226g; 郎 in s0226g is linked to Shizu.

The zan (s0264–s0268) is linked by the chapter's structure and title: 霄城 = Liu Huaizhen (made Marquis of Xiaocheng in s0088g; the horse story is s0083), 靈哲 = his son Lingzhe, 李 = Li Anmin, 王 = Wang Xuanzai; all strongly inferred.
丁、韋 (Ding and Wei), the exemplars of yielding, are surname-only allusions with no candidate and no packet information; no person rows are created.
Wenhe's aged mother (老母), mentioned only in Chang's speech, gets no person row.
耿氏 (the Geng clan), cited as a model of hereditary loyal valor, is a collective allusion and is not modeled as a person.
The rebel Zhou Panlong (州民, a provincial commoner) is not identified with Anmin's army aide Zhou Panlong of s0175; the text gives no link.
